name: UNDER PROSPERITY
materialIdentity: Forty feet of Thad's own tunnel under the worthless claim, lit by the one lamp he borrowed from his room: pick marks, packed clay, old pegged timbering somebody else left, the rock face and the gap beyond; after F3 the seam, the tended lantern and the even footprints (errata 69 A, 99 H)
note: Room 34, doc 20: under Prosperity, through the hole (24) by Thad's own tunnel (doc 57 F1). One room in two states (errata 69 A): T_BROKE_THROUGH shows the old working the way down reaches. THE GAP is the way into Room 33 (doc 57 F1); THE WAY BACK UP is the rope to the hole (errata 99 H).

exits.name: THE WAY BACK UP

LOOK_AT.say: The rope to the surface, and the coin of gray light at the top of it. Up there this is still the worthless claim. I'm in no hurry to correct anyone.
repeat: Daylight, a long way up, the size of a coin.
The coin of light has moved. It's later up there than I thought.

LISTEN_TO.say: The surface, at a great distance: wind, and the suggestion of a town.
repeat: The town. Very faint. Somebody is arguing about a boundary.
Somebody up there laughing, very far off. They don't know yet.

overrides.TALK_TO: I called up that I was all right. The gray coin of daylight did not answer, which is how daylight is.

exits.note: Doc 05: 'The rope to the surface, and the coin of gray light at the top of it.' Up to the hole (Room 23/24).

exits.name: THE GAP

LOOK_AT.say: Where my tunnel broke into a hollow in the rock. The warm air comes out of it.
repeat: Wide enough for a man who has stopped minding his coat.
Dark beyond. Not the dark of a tunnel. The dark of a room.

LISTEN_TO.say: A long, low hum, very faint. The rock is listening back.
repeat: The hum again. It does not change when I do.
Nothing I can name. I am going in to name it.

exits.note: Doc 57 F1: 'Room 34 to Room 33 is THE GAP, where the tunnel broke into a hollow.' Its lines are doc 57's.

generated.note: GENERATED. Edit the documents or the annotation, never this file.

entrances.note: Down the rope from the hole, at the foot of the shaft.

LOOK_AT.say: My father thought this was a sensible investment. He was, on the evidence, the only person in my family who has ever been right about anything.
repeat: The tines are worn bright at the ends, where I have struck it on ten thousand boot heels.
It's the only thing I own that's exactly what it claims to be.

LISTEN_TO.say: A. Four hundred and forty. It is still the only correct thing within a hundred miles.
repeat: I struck it. A, held, ringing down to nothing.
A. The same A it gave in my father's shop. Some things don't move.

LOOK_AT.say: One lamp, and about four hours of oil in it.
repeat: Three hours of oil now. I'm doing the arithmetic more often than I'd like.
It throws my shadow up the wall, three times my size and twice as confident.
A soft hiss as the wick drinks.
Burning, still. The most reassuring word in the language.

LOOK_AT.say: A lantern, not mine, hung on a spike and burned dry — years dry. Its glass is clean.
repeat: The wick has been trimmed square, the way a careful man trims one.
It hangs where it would light the way back up, not the way in. Whoever kept it always meant to leave.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Long finished. But kept, not abandoned.
repeat: Nothing. Its tin cooled a long time ago.
Nothing. It's waiting for its keeper, and its keeper isn't coming down tonight.
then: There's a difference, and you can hear it.

overrides.USE: Not mine to light. Its keeper knows where it hangs, and I find I want him to find it as he left it.

LOOK_AT.say: You can't see it, and down here that's the most interesting thing about it: the flame leans. The air is going somewhere.
repeat: Nothing to look at. There has never been anything to look at.
There's nothing to see. I keep looking anyway, like a man rereading a letter he knows by heart.
Warmer. It has been warmer every foot.
Moving, and warmer. I've stopped being surprised by it and started paying attention.
then: I've heard this before, at the top of a hole, and used it to evict a raccoon.

LOOK_AT.say: Boot prints in the clay, preserved like the creek bank's, but one pair, many visits, all the same stride. Even. He was counting.
repeat: The stride never shortens, coming or going. Whoever made these was never in a hurry and never tired.
Mine cross his now, clumsier and in a hurry. He wouldn't have approved.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. But the silence here is worn smooth, like a path.
repeat: Nothing. The clay has kept every step and repeats none of them.
Nothing. A path nobody walks any more makes exactly this sound.

LOOK_AT.say: Dark with a texture to it.
repeat: I turned the lamp down once, to see what the dark was like on its own. I turned it back up.
It isn't empty. It's only unlit.
then: The lamp makes a room the size of the lamp, and the rest of the underworld waits its turn.

LISTEN_TO.say: My own ears, ringing faintly. Underground, silence has a pitch. I could tune to it.
repeat: The ringing in my ears, settling on a note. A little flat. Of course it is.
My own heartbeat, which I have not heard in some years, keeping better time than the town.

LOOK_AT.say: The seam, where the lamp stops being casual. I've seen color in a pan, in a bottle, on a scale. I've never seen it at home before. It's different at home.
repeat: It runs at a slant into the dark, wider than my hand and further than the lamp.
I've looked at it a long time. It doesn't do anything. It doesn't need to.

LISTEN_TO.say: Not a sound. It's been keeping this quiet for longer than there have been ears.
repeat: Silence. Gold has never had to raise its voice.
Nothing. Twelve years of a town, built on top of a silence.

overrides.PICK_UP: Not with my hands. This one goes through the window, into the book, past Winnie's scales — the whole liturgy. Some gold you take; this gold I intend to file.

LOOK_AT.say: Forty feet of my own digging.
repeat: There is a bend in it where I lost my nerve and a straight stretch after where I found it again.
My pick marks are everywhere and none of them in a line. It's the most honest piece of work I've ever done.
then: It isn't square and it isn't swept, and Nickel Pratt would weep.

LISTEN_TO.say: Air. Still moving. Still going somewhere.
repeat: My own breathing, loud in here. The tunnel keeps nothing to itself.
A trickle of loose dirt from the roof, then quiet: the tunnel, settling into being a tunnel.

LOOK_AT.say: Clay, then rock, then a seam of something the lamp takes an interest in.
repeat: Rock.
Rock, mostly.
then: I'm declining to be excited. The territory has trained me thoroughly.

LISTEN_TO.say: Water, somewhere inside the stone, going about its business.
repeat: Water inside the stone again, going about its business.
Nothing I can name yet. I'm listening anyway. It's what I'm for.
Rock. I've looked at it enough to know it's rock.
Still rock.
The same small difference. It has not gone away.
Not much. Not nothing.

LOOK_AT.say: Clay, packed hard by somebody's boots long before mine.
repeat: My own prints, and the drag marks of my pick behind them.
It is level, more or less, which down here counts as hospitality.

LISTEN_TO.say: My boots, thudding, close and flat.
repeat: Grit under my heel, very loud in all this quiet.
Nothing, when I stand still. I stand still a while longer, just to hear it.

LOOK_AT.say: Old timbering, not mine, not recent. Someone was down here before the town was up there, and shored it like they meant to come back.
repeat: The joints are pegged, not nailed, by somebody who had more time than nails.
It's held a town on top of it for twelve years without a word of complaint. I know men who could learn from it.

LISTEN_TO.say: The wood takes the mountain's weight and says so, once in a while, quietly.
repeat: A long creak overhead, and then the mountain settles back.
Nothing for a while. Then one small tick, like a clock deciding not to strike.

overrides.PULL: The timber holds the mountain. I hold my curiosity. Everyone keeps their post.

lamps.note: Thad's lamp on the stump: a slow flame, nothing more (invariant 9).

figureLight.note: Errata 109, from the pre-playthrough art audit: Thad is drawn in even light so he can go in every room, and here, where the room around him averages 23.3 (of 255) against his 57, he read as pasted on. Graded to about 48, the room's surround plus 25 -- the margin the lit rooms keep -- under a warm lamp multiply gentle enough to keep his coat blue, as the Nugget's (variant B, Tyler, 2026-11-01). A measurement, not a verdict: Tyler's playthrough decides.
